text: In simulation-based medical education, the facilitator plays a key role in guiding the debriefing conversation [ 13 ]. Debriefing, described as a structured reflection aiming to explore and learn from the simulation-based experience [ 14 , 15 ], has been shown to significantly enhance clinical performance outcomes [ 16 – 20 ]. While facilitator-guided debriefing is widely regarded as the gold standard [ 13 ], learners can also lead their own reflection through self-guided debriefing [ 14 ]. In such cases, the debriefing is typically supported by cognitive aids, such as recordings of the simulation or a debriefing framework, to support self- and peer-assessment [ 14 , 21 ].
source_label: Self-guided versus facilitator-guided debriefing in immersive virtual reality simulation: Protocol for a randomized controlled non-inferiority trial assessing teamwork skills in medical students
